newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil still working on new financial tax-Malan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil still working on new financial tax-Malan.

text.p: The Brazilian government is still drawing up the small print of a new tax on financial transactions which may not be ready until next week, Finance Minister Pedro Malan said.

Malan, speaking on national Globo Network television, declined to comment on speculation that stock market investments might be exempted from the new tax, which is known by its Portuguese acronym CPMF.
"We are working (on the new tax) and I do not believe we will finish it this week," Malan told Globo.

Government officials, including Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola, have expressed concern that investors may be turned off Brazil's stock markets by the CPMF's 0.2 percent charge to be levied on financial transactions from January 23.
But the officials concede that exempting stock market investments from the CPMF would be complicated to execute and might set a precedent for other sectors wanting similar treatment.

Central Bank director Gustavo Franco said recently that foreign investors would probably have to pay the 0.2 percent charge on opening and closing an investment in Brazil but not on operations in between.

The CPMF passed through Congress earlier this year after a long campaign for its approval by then health minister Adib Jatene, who has since resigned. It is aimed at raising about $400 million a month for Brazil's ailing public health service.
